principle: Printed source facts, author-derived finite-program consequences and unproved source-class claims are different claims.

rows.meaning: For the actual ordinary quadratic, FO_A(x)=(x^T A x/2,Ax). One matvec reply plus the known query recovers FO; gradient projection recovers matvec.
rows.evidence: The full rotated A appears in f and mv. fo uses gradient f, and hactual is produced internally by actual_first_order_query. P is applied once with the continuous scalar/vector decoder and once with gradient projection.

rows.meaning: Borel query, stopping and output decisions use input-independent private randomness and past replies.
rows.evidence: next, update and initial have explicit measurability premises. P permits arbitrary measurable carriers. T fixes the literal Borel Euclidean carrier; its common seed law and program data precede every O. No direct O parameter occurs in next/update/initial. Universal representation of every source algorithm is not asserted or supplied.

rows.meaning: The source query cap is deterministic for every input and seed; it is not an expectation-budget definition.
rows.evidence: A funded request charges one interaction, a halt charges none, and an unfunded request is tagged none. The count cap is pointwise; integrability and the ordinary real expectation bound are proved afterwards.

rows.meaning: Averaging the whole private seed and taking a measurable readout yields an output law; B.1 uses a common seed law in its separate sign experiment.
rows.evidence: The exact pointwise run equality implies equality of pushforwards under the same mu. These pushforwards concern final state, Option output and actual count. They are not a sign-posterior theorem, a law containing the seed as an explicit coordinate, or a Haar-joint law.

rows.meaning: B.1 uses absorbing histories; C.1 uses dummy zero queries for a finite proof horizon.
rows.evidence: The reused interpreter stops immediately and records actual count rather than padding it to fuel. Its tagged exhaustion convention is an explicit author-derived model, not a claim that the paper defines Option-valued samples. No B.1 sign or C.1 Krylov/latent-revelation conclusion is claimed.

rows.meaning: d>=2, kappa>=2, deterministic midpoint-cosine spectrum, full orthogonal conjugation and a possibly public spectrum.
rows.evidence: Fin d has values 0,...,d-1, so (i.val+1/2)pi/d equals the paper's (i-1/2)pi/d after reindexing 1,...,d. Matrix multiplication is full O*diagonal(lambda)*O.transpose. All full real orthogonal O are quantified. No Haar distribution is asserted.

rows.meaning: The potential is the ordinary smooth quadratic with Hessian A.
rows.evidence: The producer proves HasGradientAt before identifying gradient, with the literal full matrix quadratic. T adds no genuine-gradient hypothesis. C.4 is not misattributed as the source of the FO/matvec equivalence.

rows.meaning: Class-uniform successful E-valued sampling and the Q_G query-complexity equivalence.
rows.evidence: Neither P nor T provides universal source-policy representation, a proof of some-output at sufficient fuel for all source algorithms, a Gaussian target/TV assertion, or a class-uniform Q_G theorem. This boundary is stated in the source contract, module comments, candidate assumption comparison, and lesson.

phase1_hazards.evidence: T:43-50 uses the full A action and full dot product, including off-diagonal terms.
T:41 quantifies every full orthogonal O; no determinant-component or coordinate restriction.
The same mu and program data are fixed before O in T and used for each compared pair. No random-O joint law or source-class encoding is inferred.
Programs use next S and update S Q reply; no O argument is exposed to them. Their arbitrary-state representation is explicit and is not claimed to encode all source algorithms.
The all-seed count cap precedes its expectation consequence in P:146-167 and T:60,66.
run checks halt first and stops; there are no information-bearing queries after a halt.
Omega and its sigma algebra are arbitrary; there is no uniform-seed or StandardBorel restriction.
T's f/mv are literal. The gradient is justified internally. Option none is openly an interpreter exhaustion tag, not an invented value of the source oracle or a successful Euclidean sample.
No C.1 latent history or auxiliary Gaussian vector is supplied to the program or assumed as a new premise.
No B.1 2T<n or C.1 2q+1<d threshold is imposed on P or T; their cited roles are contextual only.
Only the common-mu execution pushforwards and real count integrals are asserted; no TV supremum or Haar-average interchange is performed.
The concrete f and mv depend on A; the theorem is pointwise for each chosen orthogonal representation and asserts no canonical latent quotient.
